nodes.speaker: 旁白
nodes.text: 雷克雅未克的地热泳池冒着白雾。你刚把外套收好，窗外便在五分钟内依次出现阳光、雨和细小的冰粒。

nodes.speaker: Jón
nodes.text: Welcome to Iceland. If you don't like the weather, wait five minutes — but keep your coat nearby.

nodes.speaker: 旁白
nodes.text: 一位准备去旧港的旅行者问你下午会不会继续下雨。墙上的预报写着 showers with strong gusts。

options.text: 「There may be brief showers and strong winds this afternoon.」

nodes.speaker: Jón
nodes.text: Exactly. 'May' and 'brief' matter. A forecast describes possibility, not destiny.

nodes.speaker: Jón
nodes.text: Maybe, but the forecast says showers. Use 'may' when the sky has not made a promise.

nodes.speaker: 旁白
nodes.text: 池边广播忽然提醒：北风增强，露天区将在十分钟后暂时关闭。几位游客没有听懂，仍把毛巾留在外面。

options.text: 「The outdoor area is closing in ten minutes because of the wind.」

nodes.speaker: 旅行者
nodes.text: Thanks — the reason and the time really help. I'll get my things now.

nodes.speaker: Jón
nodes.text: Give them the time and reason too. Useful warnings answer when, what, and why.

nodes.speaker: 旁白
nodes.text: 十分钟后，风吹散了池面白雾；又过五分钟，云层裂开一道金光。所有人笑着指向刚刚被判定“糟糕”的天空。

nodes.speaker: Jón
nodes.text: See? The weather changed its mind. Good English leaves room for the world to do that.

nodes.speaker: 旁白
nodes.text: 【获得 120 金币】你学会了读天气，也学会了为不确定保留恰到好处的词。
